text: {"frames":["Olive the keeper of forgotten things has found a hall in the Tower where every dropped thimble and lost clog gathers at night, and the floor has grown wider than it was yesterday. She sweeps the wooden boards with a broom made of old reeds while the dream jars on the shelf hum a low tune. The dream-seller from the market has come to claim the hall for her glass jars, and she wants to prove the hall is hers. Olive measures the floor with her clogs, heel to toe, and counts how many square metres the forgotten things can crowd into. Which number tells you how many square metres the hall covers?","Briony, the old lock keeper, hears a soft bell from the canal beneath the Tower, and the smell of cinnamon from the waffle stalls rolls up the water stairs. In the black canal a candle flickers in a window that does not exist, and she owes that window a debt from a winter long ago. The debt can only be paid by scrubbing the floor of the lower mill hall, and she needs to know how much floor it is before she begins. She ties her apron, lifts her bucket, and steps onto the wet boards. How many square metres is the lower mill hall?","Two skaters, Jan and Sanne, are already shouting at each other on the ice of the Tower's great hall, because a line of footprints has appeared across the frozen canal overnight. Jan kicks the snow aside with his boot and points at the prints, which lead nowhere and begin nowhere. Sanne swears the prints are hers, though her skates were left at home. They agree to skate the hall from wall to wall, and whoever finds the whole floor first wins the right to call the prints theirs. The hall is wider than either of them expected. How many square metres is the ice hall where they skate?","'Your shadow is in the wrong room,' said the watchman by the dyke, who had never spoken before. Teun the traveller, who has no shadow of his own, looks down at the grey boards and sees nothing at his feet. The silent watchman waves a lantern at the wall, and a dark patch slides along the floor like spilt ink. Teun must measure the room where his shadow has been wrongly put, so the watchman can carry it back to him, and he counts the floor in long strides. How many square metres is the room where his shadow is kept?","The stork Flora stands on the Tower's top floor, and the fog around her carries a voice counting steps that are not hers. She has been called to judge a trial between two windmill keepers who each swear the hall below belongs to them. Flora lifts one leg, then the other, and waits for the voice to finish its count before she gives her verdict. She must decide the size of the hall before the fog lifts and the keepers start shouting again. What is the size of the hall in square metres?"]}
